judgements.not_verified_row_1_attempt_limit: ACCEPTED as genuinely blocked, with a narrowed reason. The gate exists and is public (orchestration.go:388-394 counts Run rows against stop_policy.max_attempts and fails 409 'task attempt limit reached'), but a task cannot accumulate attempts through the HTTP handler alone: a second claim needs the task back in READY (orchestration.go:231 allows RESUME only from BLOCKED/FAILED) and orchestration.go:236-241 refuses RESUME while any run is non-terminal; the only writers of terminal run status are reportRun/acknowledgeRunCancellation/reconcileRun (runtime.go:214-315) and every one of them requires a row in runtime_observations, whose only writer is the service method ObserveRuntime (runtime.go:113), reachable from the native coordinator (runtime_coordinator_windows.go:845) and from fixtures - there is no HTTP route that accepts an invented outcome (durability.go:220 states this). So the row is not dodged work; but it is slightly overstated: the card's own program could have called the exported ObserveRuntime the way the accepted fixtures do. It is also already covered elsewhere - I re-ran the accepted C16 selector and it PASSes C16-01/C16-02/C16-03, the no-progress counter and deferral semantics.

judgements.step_2_refused_at_START_delivered_or_not: NOT delivered as evidence, delivered as product. budget.go's admission-time chain runs inside the claim (reserveFixtureDispatch -> appendBudget -> the loop at budget.go:341-378), and my probe measured a claim refused there, so 'refused at start' is real behaviour. Those are different gates in time - the ledger-append probe proves the rule, the claim probe would prove the card's sentence. The receipt should not be registered while it calls the second one unreachable.

judgements.createTask_zero_counter_record: ACCEPTABLE as an out-of-card obligation, and the disclosure is accurate but sounds worse than the code. operations.go:184-199 looks the record up by key_hash = Hash(origin_problem_id, candidate_id, input_hash) and only mints a zero-counter NoProgressRecord when no record with that key exists, so re-creating the SAME task with the SAME inputs inherits the counter; what gets a fresh budget is genuinely different input_refs. The card's step 4 enumerates Goal/session/window, and 'changed inputs are different work' is the intended semantics (the record itself carries 'New effective evidence, changed input, or restored resource required after deferral'), so this is not an unmet requirement of this card. A trivial nonce in input_refs still resets a budget, which is a real design question - but it belongs to the card that owns operations.go.
